skill.name: zig-docs
skill.description: Fetches Zig language and standard library documentation from public sources using CLI examples for raw source, language reference, and guide content.
skill.summary: Fetch Zig standard library and language reference documentation from public Zig sources.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, visible CLI examples, and hardcoded public documentation URLs. I found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, hidden execution, or real system reconnaissance in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Network documentation fetches are implicit in the instructions.
remediation.suggestion: State that curl and pandoc should only access Zig, GitHub, and zig.guide documentation URLs, with user approval in restricted environments.

remediation.issue: Placeholder values are shown inside shell examples.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to choose module names and version tags from trusted Zig sources before replacing placeholders.

static_findings.snippet: - Zig source files contain doc comments (`//!` for module docs, `///` for item docs) that serve as a
| Std lib source | `raw.githubusercontent.com/ziglang/zig/master/lib/std/<path>` | Most reliable; in
| Language reference | `ziglang.org/documentation/master/` | Use pandoc; prose content |
Replace `master` with version tag for stable releases:
- The std lib HTML docs at ziglang.org are JavaScript-rendered and return empty content; avoid them

content.value_statement: Zig APIs and language details change quickly across versions. This skill guides agents to retrieve current documentation from Zig source, references, and guides.
actual_capabilities: Fetch Zig standard library source files with documentation comments.
Retrieve language reference pages through pandoc for readable prose.
List standard library modules using the GitHub contents API.
Find common modules such as Allocator, ArrayList, fs, json, and Build.
Search fetched source for public functions, types, and documentation comments.
Switch documentation URLs from master to a specific Zig release tag.
limitations: Requires network access to GitHub, ziglang.org, or zig.guide.
Requires local CLI tools such as curl, pandoc, jq, grep, and head for examples.
Does not parse JavaScript-rendered standard library HTML pages.
Does not verify that retrieved documentation matches a local Zig compiler version.

use_cases.title: Check Standard Library APIs
use_cases.description: Fetch a Zig standard library module and inspect public function signatures before editing code.

use_cases.title: Compare Versioned Documentation
use_cases.description: Replace master with a release tag to inspect documentation for a stable Zig version.

use_cases.title: Explain Language Features
use_cases.description: Retrieve the language reference as plain text and summarize relevant sections for implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch a Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one library module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the Zig standard library documentation for std.mem and summarize the main allocator-related APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused search inside one source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up std.mem.Allocator.create in the Zig documentation and explain its signature, parameters, and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Version Tag
prompt_templates.scenario: Stable documentation lookup for a release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Zig 0.14.0 documentation to check std.log behavior and report any relevant API details.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reference and Source
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the Zig language reference and relevant standard library source for error handling, then reconcile any differences.

output_examples.output: The response identifies the Allocator source file, summarizes the create function, and explains allocation errors in plain language.

output_examples.input: List standard library modules related to file system work.
output: The response names likely modules such as fs and fs.File.
It explains which source files to fetch for deeper details.

output_examples.input: Explain Zig defer from the language reference.
output_examples.output: The response fetches reference prose, summarizes defer behavior, and notes where ordering matters.

best_practices: Use version tags when the project depends on a stable Zig release.
Prefer raw standard library source when HTML documentation is incomplete.
Fetch only the specific module or reference section needed for the task.
anti_patterns: Do not assume master branch documentation matches every local compiler version.
Do not rely on JavaScript-rendered standard library pages for complete content.
Do not paste untrusted module names into shell commands without checking them.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents retrieve and inspect Zig documentation from public source and reference pages.

faq.question: Does it install Zig or other packages?
faq.answer: No. It only provides command examples for fetching documentation with existing CLI tools.

faq.question: Which documentation sources does it use?
faq.answer: It points to raw Zig source on GitHub, the Zig language reference, zig.guide, and GitHub release tags.

faq.question: Can it use release-specific documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace master in the URL with a Zig release tag, such as 0.14.0.

faq.question: Why use raw source files?
faq.answer: Zig source files include documentation comments and are reliable when rendered HTML pages are incomplete.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands fetch public documentation from GitHub, ziglang.org, or zig.guide.
